description: A quantum error-correcting code: stabilizer generators and separate lists of logical X and Z operators. The number of logical qubits equals the length of the `x` array. Loading preserves unequal X/Z list lengths and algebraic errors for audit; the schema checks structure and Pauli token spelling only.

stabilizers.description: Stabilizer generators in Pauli sparse format. Addressed by index (e.g. `in[0].stabilizers[0]` for the first input encoding). May be over-complete (linearly dependent).

x.description: Logical X operators, one entry per logical qubit. Array index determines the logical qubit index (e.g. `in[0].x[0]` is the first logical qubit's X operator in the first input encoding). Audit checks that this list has the same length as `z`.

z.description: Logical Z operators, one entry per logical qubit. Audit checks that this list has the same length as `x`.

metadata.description: Optional free-form annotations. qodec carries this object through load and save unchanged and never interprets it (though it does participate in structural equality). Use it for tool- or author-specific data (timings, provenance, tags, vendor hints). qodec reserves no keys; namespacing by tool (e.g. an `acme` or `ibm` sub-object) is a recommendation, not a rule.

Pauli.description: An unsigned Pauli operator as whitespace-separated tokens, e.g. `X_0 Z_1 Y_2`. Each token is I, X, Y, or Z with an optional `_index` suffix; a missing suffix means index zero. Indexes allow leading zeros and a leading `+`, as in `X_+01`. Neither `+` nor `-` may precede the basis. Empty and whitespace-only strings are accepted. The schema checks token spelling; the Rust code loader additionally requires indexes smaller than `usize::MAX` so the code dimension is representable. Algebra is checked by audit, not by this schema or code loading. Instruction actions preserve Pauli text without these code-token checks.
